clue.text: Cheer snob somehow beginning to get composer

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of these words are arranged in some other way
beginning to asks for only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A snooty music lover cheers, and is somehow prompted to take up a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' shuffles CHEER SNOB; 'beginning to' takes the G of 'get' for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Schoenberg was the Austrian creator of twelve-tone music.

clue.text: Set point lost, but make quick progress

indicators.note: lost suggests these letters have gone astray and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player throws away a set point but must hurry on.
explanation.walkthrough: A set point is the point that would win a set in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom meaning hurry up, originally to press the accelerator.

clue.text: Exciting bottom seen in place of undesirable activity

parts.note: hot means exciting, sensational
a bed is the bottom, as of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A racy rear view caught in a seedy spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' tempts a cheeky reading, but it is a river or sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is an environment where something, usually bad such as crime, thrives.

clue.text: Bad blood from European with German in New York

indicators.note: in says the German word sits inside the letters for New York

parts.note: mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A feud between two people abroad in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or ill feeling, which bad blood names as an idiom.

clue.text: Wager Ireland should accept no abomination

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: should accept says the word for Ireland takes the other word inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A gamble that Ireland will refuse to accept a hated thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bete noire is a person or thing especially loathed, from the French for black beast.

clue.text: Ignore flying doctor giving war cry

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are scattered in the air and reassembled

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A flying doctor ignores a shout of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying doctor' looks like one Australian air service, but 'flying' works on 'Ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache leader's name became the shout paratroopers gave when jumping.

clue.text: Parrot shy about pelican at first

indicators.note: about says the word for shy goes round the other piece

parts.note: shy means coy, bashful

indicators.note: at first asks for just the opening letter of the bird's name

explanation.surface: A shy parrot keeps its distance from a pelican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a verb here, to mimic, not the bird the pelican suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate exactly, which is what making a duplicate does.

clue.text: What's white and sparkling as teeth?

definitions.meaning: a description of a sparkling white wine, champagne in casual British slang
the teeth one champs or chews with

explanation.surface: A riddle comparing a dazzling smile with fizzy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The riddle shape suggests one thing, but each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is jocular British slang for champagne, and teeth champ food.

clue.text: PM, English, gives first performance

parts.note: PM is the Prime Minister, also called the premier

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister makes a debut appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To premiere a show is to stage it publicly for the very first time.

clue.text: Reckon to have one million in assets

indicators.note: in says these letters are placed inside the word for assets

parts.note: an estate is the whole of someone's assets
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they hold a million in assets.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon a figure is to calculate it roughly, a rough judgement of value.

clue.text: Harvester in back-breaking exercise?

indicators.note: breaking says the exercise splits the word for back open

parts.note: the rear is the back
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A farmhand with a scythe doing back-breaking work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-breaking' reads as one adjective describing hard labour, but the hyphenated word splits into a piece and its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper is a person or machine that cuts and gathers crops.

clue.text: Subtle quality — or unsubtle one!

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden, the opposite of subtle

explanation.surface: A wry remark that something is either subtle or blatant.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied nuance, a suggestion lying beneath the main meaning.

clue.text: Pot knocked over: relatives will get serviette

indicators.note: knocked over says the word for pot is turned upside down, read backwards in this across light

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A dinner mishap: a pot is upset and family members are handed something to mop up.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette is the British word for a table linen square used at meals.

clue.text: White magician conceals object

indicators.note: conceals says the letters are tucked inside the words that come before it

explanation.surface: A good magician makes something disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or article, a synonym of object.

clue.text: Bats are able to develop

indicators.note: bats here means crazy, so the following letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Flying mammals are capable of evolving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals but is the slang adjective for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to work out in detail, expanding or building up an idea.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about says the word for row goes round the word for stray

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a wandering dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, plucky hunting dog.

clue.text: Unfortunately meet Bond, getting buried

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things go wrong for these letters, which are jumbled

explanation.surface: An enemy who unluckily runs into James Bond ends up in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombed means placed in a tomb, laid to rest underground.

clue.text: Communist annoyed humanitarian organisation

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A leftist irritated by an aid agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international movement providing medical and disaster relief.

clue.text: Common person seen in theatre, very mannered

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An ordinary playgoer is noticed at a show, acting affectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Everyman is also a medieval morality play.
explanation.definitionFit: An everyman is an ordinary, typical person, the man in the street.

clue.text: Throw back tailless crustacean

parts.note: to lob is to throw high

indicators.note: tailless says the final letter of the word for back is cut off

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to toss a shellfish without a tail back into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a large clawed marine shellfish.

clue.text: Less well entertained by some light banter

indicators.note: entertained by says the first piece is held within the second

parts.note: a ray is a beam, some light
iller means sicker, less well

explanation.surface: A poorly person is cheered by gentle teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing, a near synonym of banter.

clue.text: Star returned in luggage van

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A celebrity is sent back on the baggage wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AGEV, hidden across 'luggage van', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: One doing badly shows colour

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the word before it are put in poor order

explanation.surface: Someone performing poorly reveals their true colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is the deep blue-violet hue between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Scholar took exam, securing first place

indicators.note: securing says the exam word holds the other piece

parts.note: sat means took an exam
the van is the front, first place

explanation.surface: A student sat a test and came top.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, especially a distinguished academic.

clue.text: Tory and scoundrel are in agreement

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories
a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician and a rogue see eye to eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to agree, so a plural subject that concurs is united in view.

clue.text: Old sailors with invitation to go round duchy

indicators.note: to go round says the invitation word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a call is an invitation to visit
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Retired seamen are invited on a tour of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall, England's south-western tip, is a royal duchy held by the heir to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duchy of Cornwall is the estate that supports the monarch's eldest son.

clue.text: Answer Joycean protagonist having come out

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's Ulysses

explanation.surface: A reply from the hero of a Joyce novel who has made a public revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having come out' suggests a confession, but it means flowers opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers in bloom have opened, which is what it means for buds to come out.

clue.text: Drollery less desirable as one gets on?

parts.note: bad means undesirable, unwelcome
getting on means growing older, so this is in age

explanation.surface: Someone ruefully notes that wit sours with the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, witty banter, the light humour that drollery names.

clue.text: Fateful day — team heading into last place

indicators.note: heading into last place says the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a side is a sporting team

explanation.surface: A doomed day as a club tumbles to the bottom of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March was the date Julius Caesar was murdered, famously warned about by a soothsayer.

clue.text: Remarkable new town theory

indicators.note: new says the letters of these words are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A striking new theory of urban planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noteworthy deserves attention, the same as being worth remarking on.
